top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct operating principle: the magic-wavelength condition removes the trap-induced shift of the clock transition, so a large neutral-atom ensemble combines the statistics of many atoms with accuracy once reserved for single ions. It is mature, with fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 reproduced and intercompared across independent laboratories. The Katori and Ye pair is the cleanest credit available, and a species-neutral citation isolating the magic-wavelength lattice answers the overlap objection with the 2005 and 2012 prizes. No award is clearly weaker than this ripe, well-scoped achievement.
